claim: Deleting the already-merged migration 1780592070031-ConvertNegativeRatingToNull.ts makes any database that recorded it fail to boot: kysely's #ensureNoMissingMigrations throws 'corrupted migrations' before the allowUnorderedMigrations gate, runMigrations() rethrows, and nothing up the bootstrap chain catches it — instances restart-loop until the kysely_migrations row is hand-deleted. Additionally, instances that ran the migration already had -1 ratings converted to NULL in place with a no-op down(), so that data is irreversibly lost and the change ships nothing to reconcile or acknowledge it.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: Deleting the already-merged `ConvertNegativeRatingToNull` migration makes any database that ran it fail to boot

claim: metadata.service.ts:308 still uses validateRange(exifTags.Rating, 1, 5), so a -1 rating accepted by PUT /assets/:id is silently reset to NULL by the server's own job pipeline: updateExif locks rating and queues SidecarWrite, handleSidecarWrite writes Rating:-1 to XMP then unlocks rating, onDone chains AssetExtractMetadata, which reads the sidecar's -1, validateRange returns null, and upsertExif with lockedPropertiesBehavior 'skip' overwrites -1 with NULL because it is no longer locked. Only asset.dto.ts of the four files 99281de restricted was reverted; the deleted unit and e2e negative-rating tests are not restored.
raw: #2 🔴 Critical: A `-1` rating accepted by the API is silently reset to NULL by the server's own job pipeline

claim: Replacing .min(1).max(5) with a .refine() predicate on UpdateAssetDto.rating and AssetBulkUpdateDto.rating erases the bound from the generated OpenAPI spec (minimum/maximum become ±9007199254740991), so the published contract says 'any safe integer' while the server enforces {-1} ∪ [1,5]; client generators lose request-side validation and the Dart model documents Minimum value: -9007199254740991. Suggested fix: z.union([z.literal(-1), z.int().min(1).max(5)]) or .meta({minimum:-1, maximum:5}).
raw: #3 🟠 High: Moving the bound into `.refine()` erases it from the published OpenAPI contract

claim: BaseSearchSchema.rating in search.dto.ts still has .min(1).max(5) (not reverted from 99281de), so /search/metadata, /search/random, /search/smart and statistics search reject rating:-1 with 400 and rejected assets can be set but never found (rating:null matches genuinely unrated assets instead); the regenerated OpenAPI spec is now self-contradicting, with Update/BulkUpdate DTOs saying '0 is no longer valid' and search DTOs saying '-1 is no longer valid' in the same v3. Suggested fix: extract one shared ratingSchema used by both.
raw: #4 🟠 High: Search DTOs still reject `-1`, so rejected assets can be set but never found — and the spec now contradicts itself

claim: ExifResponseSchema.rating in exif.dto.ts still declares z.int().min(1).max(5).nullish().default(null) (tightened by 99281de, not reverted), and mapExif passes entity.rating through unclamped, so GET /assets/:id for a -1-rated asset returns exifInfo.rating:-1 in violation of the published response schema; no runtime failure today because ZodSerializerInterceptor is inert without a @ZodSerializerDto, but it would fail or coerce the day one is added.
raw: #5 🟡 Medium: The EXIF response contract still declares `[1-5]`, so the server can return a `-1` that violates its own published schema

claim: Duplicate merge in duplicate.service.ts:258-267 computes let rating = 0; if (assetRating > rating) …; if (rating > 0) response.exifUpdate.rating = rating, so merging a rejected (-1) duplicate into an unrated (null) keeper never propagates the -1 — the rejection is silently lost and the rejected duplicate is trashed. Pre-existing code the change makes reachable again; tiered down for single finder / screen score 60.

The change removes the shipped v2.6.0 history entry ('Using -1 as a rating is deprecated…') from the asset DTO rating schema, silently rewriting a statement that shipped in the v2.6.0 spec; arguably correct since -1 is no longer deprecated — judged a judgment call, not a verifiable defect.
raw: Removal of the shipped `v2.6.0` history entry ("Using -1 as a rating is deprecated…").

claim: The new v3 history text 'Using 0 as a rating is no longer valid' on the asset DTO rating field was checked against the pre-99281de schema (0 was coerced to null, now rejected with 400) and found factually accurate — no defect.
raw: New `v3` history text "Using 0 as a rating is no longer valid".

claim: The Zod chain ordering .int().nullable().refine(…).optional() on rating was probed against the repo's Zod: {}, null, -1, 3 pass; 0, 6, -2, 3.5 reject with expected messages — behaviorally equivalent to the old .nullish() for absent/null cases, no defect.

The generated Dart client's minimum: -9007199254740991 bound is only in a doc comment on Optional<int?> rating with no runtime validation, and Dart int is 64-bit — no numeric overflow; the impact reduces to lost client-side validation already covered by the OpenAPI-bound finding.
media.repository.ts:118 (Rating: tags.rating === null ? 0 : tags.rating) was traced; a -1 rating passes through unchanged — no defect.
raw: `media.repository.ts:118` (`Rating: tags.rating === null ? 0 : tags.rating`) — traced; `-1` passes through unchanged.

claim: A live response-serialization 500 on returning -1 does not occur today because the globally registered ZodSerializerInterceptor is inert without any @ZodSerializerDto in the codebase; downgraded from a live failure to the ExifResponseSchema contract defect.
